title: Closer (m/f) - Investor Relations in Düsseldorf
description:
Late shift. High stakes. Six US time zones. One shot per call.

This is a genuine job posting - not a ghost job!

Let's skip the part where we tell you this is “an exciting opportunity in a dynamic environment.” You've read that sentence four hundred times and seen it all.

Here's what's actually true:

We need an experienced, financially literate Closer who speaks English on a native or C2 Level, can pick up a phone at 3:30pm, talk to a stranger with eight figures in a brokerage account somewhere in Wyoming or Connecticut, get them to sign a convertible promissory note before their assistant walks in with coffee. That's it. That's the job. Everything else is detail.

Who We Are

Meridion AG runs the show from Monheim & Düsseldorf. Our US arm, Meridion Dynamics Inc., builds intelligent software and smart energy technology. But you're not selling the product. You're closing the investment that funds it. Different animal, different muscle.

Aufgaben

What You'll Actually Do

  • Take warm(ish) leads from our setters - accredited US investors who already know we called - and close them on convertible promissory notes.
  • Walk investors through the accreditation process without losing them to paperwork fatigue.
  • Hold the line, know the terms cold, and answer the “wait, what happens if you don't hit your IPO timeline” question without blinking.
  • If a setter is running low on appointments, out sick or on vacation, you step in and run up to 100 outbound cold calls that day to convert cold leads into your Closing appointments. Yes, a hundred. We count :)
  • Talk to people who have people and AI to screen their calls - and get past their Gatekeepers.

Qualifikation

What You Bring

  • Real closing experience - several years of it, in high-ticket sales, investment products, or anything else where “no” is the opening bid, not the final answer. This is not a rookie position.
  • English at a genuine native level. Not “I watched a lot of Suits.” You need to sound like you belong in a room with a family office CFO. If it's not your first language, we're talking true C2, no exceptions. An accent is no Dealbreaker but your vocabulary, your pronunciation, the way you use idioms - your vibe on the phone - must be on fleek.
  • A voice and presence that reads as calm, unbothered, and confident - think less “modern hustle culture” - more Brian Tracy.
  • Genuine understanding of what an accredited investor is, what a convertible note does, and why someone would put $50k+ into one. We'll brief you thoroughly - but you need financial literacy to keep up from day one.
  • A working understanding of US investor culture, even sitting in Düsseldorf’s Seestern District.

Benefits

The Deal

  • Full-time, 40h/week, onsite at our Düsseldorf office near Seestern.
  • Late shift: 2:30pm - 10pm, because your workday runs on Pacific and Eastern time, not Berlin time.
  • Base salary + commission
  • Onboarding is real: Expect a genuine ramp-up before you're fully solo on calls.
  • Start: ASAP - which translates to “realistically September/October”.

Not For You If

You cling to a script forever to feel confident. You've never been told “no” 70 times in a day and called it Tuesday. You think “Closer” means you show up after someone else already did the hard part.

Sound like your Tuesday? Send us your CV.
We don’t do 5 interview rounds.
You talk to me on the phone or in a brief Teams Video Call.

If I sense you’re a fit, we’ll welcome you onsite for another brief interview with our CEO; please plan in approximately 2h for the interview, a brief vibe check with the team and one or two test calls so we can hear your closing performance.

That’s it.

As our Senior Concept Creative, you’ll join our Brand team, where we own the brand core: what we stand for, how we sound and the stories we tell. Your Profile

  • You’re a storyteller. You find the story in a product and make people care about it, and you understand how stories travel across countries such as France, Italy, Spain and the US.

  • You think in big ideas, and you know why they’ll work and how they’ll sell. You come up with lots of ideas quickly, dare to pitch the crazy ones, know which one to fight for, and take feedback as fuel, not criticism.

  • You write short, sharp copy in fluent English, and you know the difference between a nice line and one that sells.

  • You’ve worked on launches or campaigns with sales targets and understand promotions, retail and marketplaces. You use campaign and channel performance (paid social hooks, CRM, PDP conversion, influencer reach) to learn which stories sell, and feed that into the next concept.

title: Staff Platform Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Our goal is to have a solar system on every roof, a storage unit in every house, and an electric car in every garage. Enpal makes this possible with an integrated total solution for decentralized energy—from solar systems and battery storage to wall boxes, smart meters, and heat pumps. At the heart of it all is our AI-powered platform Enpal.One+, which intelligently connects thousands of systems and efficiently optimizes electricity procurement and feed-in on the energy market.

Are you ready for solutions that are more than just a promise and bring real quality of life to thousands of households every day? What you create at Enpal will deliver clean electricity tomorrow and bring about lasting change in how we use energy.

Job Description

As a Staff Platform Engineer, you will provide technical leadership for the internal platform that powers Enpal's applications and services. You will set technical direction, raise the bar on engineering standards, and drive cross-team initiatives that make our platform more reliable, secure, and scalable. You'll partner closely with engineering leadership, senior platform engineers, and development teams, acting as a force multiplier through mentorship, architectural guidance, and hands-on contribution to the platform's hardest problems.

 

This role is ideal for engineers who have deep, proven expertise in platform and cloud engineering and want to shape the technical strategy of a growing engineering organization, not just execute within it.

At Enpal, you would be:

  • Owning platform architecture. Define and evolve the architecture of our internal platform, making build-vs-buy and long-term design decisions that balance reliability, scalability, security, and cost.

  • Driving infrastructure automation at scale. Lead the design of automation and self-service tooling that removes manual toil across deployment, provisioning, and operations for the whole engineering org, not just your own team.

  • Setting technical standards. Establish best practices for Kubernetes operations, CI/CD pipelines, observability, and infrastructure as code, and ensure they are adopted consistently across teams.

  • Elevating the developer experience. Treat the platform as a product for internal teams: drive usability, reliability, and documentation improvements that let engineers ship faster and safer, and define the metrics that prove it.

  • Mentoring and growing engineers. Coach platform and junior engineers, review designs and code, and raise the overall technical level of the team through pairing, documentation, and feedback.

  • Leading complex, cross-team initiatives. Take ownership of high-impact projects that span multiple teams, from scoping and design through rollout, with minimal oversight.

  • Driving continuous improvement. Proactively identify risks, inefficiencies, and technical debt, and lead the changes that materially improve stability, performance, and automation.

  • Partnering across the organization. Work closely with developers, operations, security, and leadership to understand real needs and translate them into platform solutions and roadmap priorities.

Qualifications

We are looking for an experienced engineer with deep technical expertise, strong judgment, and a track record of leading platform initiatives.

  • 8+ years of experience in platform, cloud, DevOps, or software engineering roles, including significant time operating production systems at scale.

  • Proven, hands-on expertise with cloud environments and containerized applications (Azure, Kubernetes and more), including designing and operating production-grade clusters.

  • Deep experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), CI/CD tooling, Helm and observability tooling, with the judgment to choose the right approach for a given problem.

  • A demonstrated track record of leading technical initiatives end to end, from design through rollout, across multiple teams.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar of a team, including through code/design review and documentation.

  • Strong system design skills, with the ability to reason about trade-offs in reliability, scalability, security, and cost.

  • Clear communication skills in English, spoken and written, with the ability to influence stakeholders at multiple levels. Knowledge of German is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • Experience setting up or scaling platform teams in a fast-growing organization.

  • Deep understanding of monitoring, alerting, and incident response practices, including on-call ownership and postmortems.

  • Contributions to open-source platform or infrastructure tooling.

  • Experience operating in regulated or compliance-sensitive environments (e.g., energy, fintech).

Are you interested even if you don't meet all the requirements? Apply anyway! We look forward to discovering your potential—regardless of whether your experience meets every single requirement. ☀️

What we offer

  • Work at Germany's first green unicorn - Play an active role in shaping the solar energy transition.

  • The sun shines all over the world - At Enpal, you'll work with a highly motivated, diverse team of over 65 nationalities.

  • The ideal setup for your focus - We are convinced that excellent results are achieved when the conditions are right. That's why we rely on a hybrid working concept that gives you the freedom to always work in the way that best suits your tasks. Do you need new inspiration on an international level? With Workflex, we offer you the opportunity to relocate abroad for up to 30 days a year, depending on your responsibilities.

  • Grown-up business & startup spirit - In our modern office in Berlin-Friedrichshain, you'll find everything your heart desires, from height-adjustable desks and table tennis to stocked beverage fridges and barista coffee.

  • Your kick-start at Enpal - Onboarding day with a welcome bag, buddy program, and a team that really supports you.

  • Stay up to date & help shape the future - Transparent all-hands meetings, short decision-making processes, and an open feedback culture - without mistakes, there is no progress.

  • The energy transition can only be achieved together - At Enpal, you can expect legendary team spirit and unforgettable team events.

  • Your extra boost - 29 vacation days + one additional day off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, discounted membership at Wellhub, and corporate benefits. Everything you need to help you achieve a good work-life balance.

  • Investing in your future – We don’t just think sustainably when it comes to energy, but also when it comes to you. Take advantage of our company pension scheme to build a solid foundation for your future, step by step.

  • Make your home smart – Sustainability starts at your doorstep. As part of our team, you’ll benefit from a permanent 25% discount on the entire Bosch Smart Home product range – for an even more efficient and connected home.

At Enpal, we are proud of the diversity of our team. No decisions are made on the basis of skin colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability or age, either during recruitment or employment. Enpal stands for a safe workplace and takes action against discrimination and harassment of any kind.

title: Creative Director (m/w/d)
description:
Über Teaching Socials

Teaching Socials ist die führende Unternehmensberatung für Personal Brands im Finanz- & Immobilienbereich im DACH-Raum. Unser Team aus 25 High-Performern hat innerhalb von 2 Jahren ein konstantes Monatswachstum von über 750.000 € aufgebaut. Wir verbinden Sichtbarkeit, Kundenakquise und Unternehmenswachstum in einem System – und du sorgst mit deinen Videos dafür, dass aus Ideen Reichweite, aus Zuschauern qualifizierte Leads und aus unserer eigenen Marke messbare Ergebnisse werden.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Content-Strategie: Du entwickelst für uns einen Content-Plan für die nächsten Wochen und leitest daraus einen klaren Produktionsplan für die Cutter ab.

  • Ideen und Skripte: Du findest die Themen, Hooks und Titel für alle Hauptvideos auf YouTube und schreibst die Skripte selbst.

  • Dreh: Du begleitest Drehs, verstehst Kamera, Licht und Ton und greifst selbst zur Kamera, wenn es nötig ist.

  • Schnitt und Qualität: Du gibst jedes Video frei, bevor es online geht. Was nicht gut genug ist, geht zurück.

  • Cutter-Führung: Du führst das Cutter-Team, gibst regelmäßig konkretes Feedback und machst jeden Editor messbar besser.

  • Shortform und Ads: Du sorgst dafür, dass aus jedem Longform-Video verwertbare Clips und Ad-Creatives entstehen.

  • Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung: Du führst die Weeklys, erklärst, was produziert wird und warum, und vertrittst deine Entscheidungen auch dann, wenn jemand anders denkt.

Was für dich drin ist

  • Reichweite ab Tag eins: Du arbeitest mit einer der größten Educational-Creator-Marken im DACH-Raum

  • Starkes Team: Familiäres Umfeld, gemeinsame Erfolge und Geburtstage

  • Schnelle Wege: Deine Ideen werden intern umgesetzt, statt in endlosen Entscheidungsschleifen zu versanden

  • Direkter Impact: Deine Videos beeinflussen unmittelbar Reichweite, Leads und Umsätze

  • Führung: Du führst ein eigenes Cutter-Team und prägst, wie bei uns Content entsteht

Das bringst du mit

  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung als Content Creator, Video Producer oder Head of Content, idealerweise mit Fokus auf YouTube-Longform, Shortform und Video-Ads

  • Ein Portfolio mit Videos, die du verantwortet hast, idealerweise mit messbaren Ergebnissen wie Views, Klickrate und Zuschauerbindung

  • Fundiertes Verständnis dafür, was ein Video viral macht: Hook, Titel, Thumbnail, Storytelling und Retention

  • Starkes Gespür für Ideen und Skripte: Du schreibst YouTube-Skripte selbst, die Zuschauer bis zum Ende halten

  • Editing auf hohem Niveau: Longform, Shortform und cinematic – idealerweise bist du selbst Creator

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Kamera, Licht und Ton: Du kannst selbst drehen

  • Verständnis für Video-Ads und ihre Rolle im Funnel und in der Customer Journey

  • Sicherer Umgang mit relevanten Kennzahlen wie CTR, Zuschauerbindung, Views und CPL

  • Führungserfahrung: Du steuerst mehrere Cutter gleichzeitig, planst Produktion und gibst Feedback, das dein Team besser macht

  • Souveräne Kommunikation: Du führst Weeklys und vertrittst deine Content-Entscheidungen auch gegenüber den Foundern

  • Hohe Standards: Kein Video verlässt dein Team, hinter dem du nicht selbst stehst

  • Eigenverantwortung: Du wartest nicht auf Ansagen, sondern bringst eigene Ideen und Trends ein

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau

  • Ein Plus: Erfahrung mit Podcast- und Event-Drehs sowie tiefes Technik-Verständnis (Kamera-Setups, Equipment, Workflows)

Du passt eher nicht zu uns, wenn …

  • du lieber schöne Bilder produzierst, statt Videos, die Reichweite und Nachfrage erzeugen

title: Technical Product Manager - Developer Experience (DevEx)
description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Your mission is to make it dramatically easier for our engineers to ship features and learn from them quickly, securely, and reliably. You'll aim for small-startup speed while meeting the quality bar of a large financial institution. Velocity here means removing friction and toil from the path between idea and learning, not asking people to work harder.

AI is a big part of the opportunity, and we're looking for a PM who is optimistic about its possibilities but pragmatic about what actually works. The goal is not to adopt the latest shiny AI tool; it's to deeply understand your internal users, experiment, and honestly evaluate what solves their problems, whether that's AI, process changes, or boring tooling that just works.

The Technical Product Manager - DevEx will:

  • Lead a team of engineers with full ownership of how we deliver new features for our users and use AI solutions to remove impactful friction for our engineers and product managers.

  • Directly manage the DevEx team to help them grow in their careers, partnering with the Tech Lead, who will own the technical bar.

Key Details

  • This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, USA (East Coast), Canada, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso
  • Wave is a distributed team, and we fund up to three in-person get-togethers a year, in line with Wave's travel policy.

About Product at Wave

Product has always been very important to us at Wave, starting from day one with two very strong product-minded founders. Product Managers play a central role in our organization, impacting large chunks of the company around them, similar to the founders they were shaped after years ago.

Our approach to building products may not be what you've seen in other places. Our processes are lightweight, informed by principles instead of methodologies and our PMs don't just manage backlogs full of polished tickets. Read our write-up on product at Wave!

This role owns making that network work. That means the right pitstops, at a pay that works for them and for us. When one goes wrong, you see it the same day in parcels left behind and routes running late. You’ll build the systems that stop that happening, and fix it fast when it does.

title: Junior Software Developer
description:
The Software Developer I, Connector role supports Trial Interactive’s proprietary platform, Connector - the cloud-based integrations that move life science data between clients’ clinical systems (for example EDC/eCRF and IRT systems) and Trial Interactive’s life science products. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, the role helps build and maintain connectors, keeps client data flowing accurately, and resolves issues when it does not.

This is a blended role, covering development and maintenance up until handling client requests. This role works closely with the Solutions, DevOps and Engineering teams.

DESCRIPTION

As part of the Development and maintenance responsibility, the resource handles:

• Develop, test and maintain connector components in C# on .NET (AWS Lambda), including the parsers and mappers that convert source-system data (API payloads, files) into the formats required by the Trial Interactive CTMS and eTMF.

• Configure and extend mappings for new studies, sites and visit/status definitions on existing connectors, reusing existing modules wherever possible.

• Assist in the technical onboarding of new clients and studies: connector configuration, test runs in non-production environments, and verification before go-live.

• Work with the AWS services connectors are built on (Lambda, SQS, S3, EventBridge/Step Functions, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and make small, reviewed infrastructure changes using Terraform under supervision.

• Consume, test and troubleshoot REST APIs (client/vendor APIs and Trial Interactive import APIs) using code and tools such as Postman, and help extend APIs that improve connector stability and connectivity.

• Write unit and functional tests; use Git (feature branches, merge requests, environment branches) and follow the team’s code review and release process.

• Keep code, configuration and change records documented so that others can maintain them.

• Work on special projects, such as local test environments using LocalStack.

As part of handling Client communication, support and ticket resolution, the resource does:

• Own assigned support tickets from triage to closure: reproduce the issue, investigate, fix or escalate, and record the outcome in the ticketing system (for example Jira, ServiceDesk Plus).

• Investigate data issues end to end – trace a record from the source payload through the archive, parser, connector database and logs to its CTMS/eTMF import result – and establish the root cause (RCA) with evidence.

• Reconcile source-system data against the CTMS/eTMF when a client reports missing or mismatched subjects, visits or statuses, and explain any differences.

• Communicate with clients and Solutions Engineers by email, tickets and calls: acknowledge requests promptly, ask clear clarifying questions, give regular status updates, and explain findings and next steps in plain language.

• Monitor connector health (CloudWatch logs, failed imports, notifications) and respond to failures within agreed response times.

• Escalate appropriately to senior engineers, DevOps or the vendor, with a concise summary of what happened, when, in which environment and for which records.

• Write up RCAs, fixes and known issues so that repeat problems are resolved faster, and help keep support documentation current.

• Handle client and clinical data with care: use the minimum data needed, never share one client’s information with another, and follow Trial Interactive data-protection and change-control procedures.

General

• Keep learning the connector platform, the clinical-trial data domain and cloud and software development best practices.

• Complete all other tasks that are deemed appropriate for this role and assigned by the manager/supervisor.


REQUIRED SKILLS

• Clear written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical issues in plain language to non-technical clients and to write concise ticket updates and emails.

• A client-service mindset: responsive, calm under pressure, and takes ownership of a ticket until it is resolved or properly handed over.

• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills: forms a hypothesis, checks logs and data, and proves the root cause with evidence before concluding.

• Strong attention to detail with data, such as identifiers, dates, time zones and character encodings.

• Good time management: balances planned development work with interrupt-driven support, prioritizing by client impact.

• Works collaboratively within a team, asks for help early, and is self-motivated and eager to learn.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• 0–1 years of experience in software development, technical support or cloud-based application support; internships and substantial academic or personal projects count.

• Working knowledge of C# and the .NET framework: able to read and debug existing code and deliver small features.

• Familiarity with AWS, particularly Lambda, S3, SQS and CloudWatch Logs.

• Working SQL skills (joins, filtering, aggregation) on relational databases, preferably MySQL.

• Understanding of REST APIs and of JSON, XML and CSV data; experience calling APIs with Postman or similar tools.

• Understanding of data parsing and mapping techniques, including handling of dates, null values and encodings.

• Experience or familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git).

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• Experience with LocalStack for local AWS cloud application development.

• Familiarity with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code tools.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation.

• Prior experience in customer-facing support, or with ticketing tools such as Jira or ServiceDesk Plus.

• Exposure to clinical research systems and concepts (EDC, CTMS, eTMF; study, site, subject, visit) or to regulated (GxP) software environments.

• Scripting (Python or shell) for data checks and log analysis.

• Familiarity with containerization and microservices architecture.

title: Lead Product Designer
description:
Lead Product Designer

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)

💰 £70k-£90k (negotiable)

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group

  • Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

  • Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

  • Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

  • Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

  • You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

  • You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

  • You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

  • You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

  • You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

  • You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

  • You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

  • You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you

  • Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

  • Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

  • AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

  • Craft: Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach. You have views on interaction quality, hierarchy, motion, microcopy - and you can defend them.

  • Cross-functional: Comfortable as a peer at the table with product and engineering counterparts in your domain. Drive direction; don't wait for it.

  • Open to flex: This is predominantly an IC role, but we're not rigid about it. If you've line-managed before, or want to take on one or two direct reports alongside the IC work, we're open to that conversation.

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

Why join Street Group?

🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week

🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!)

💪 Joining a culture that supports your development and encourages growth

🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured

🧘 Regular well-being initiatives

🕒 Flexible working hours

🌷 Paid menopause leave

🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition

👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day

👩🏿‍💻 A chance to work on cutting-edge technology

🐶 Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome!

🍻 Fully stocked fridge and beers (or an alternative) on us every Friday afternoon

🎊 Company and team off-sites, events and happy hours

🚴 Cycle to work scheme

🚗 Electric car salary sacrifice scheme

🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company!

Salary

We don't have a fixed band published for this role yet - it'll be calibrated based on your experience and scope. Please apply and let's have the conversation.

Interview Process

We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Menlo Security is the leader in Browser Security for human and agentic workforces. Our mission is to enable humans and agents to connect, communicate, and collaborate securely, without compromise. The Menlo Browser Security Platform protects organizations from cyberattacks by stopping threats across the web, documents, and email before they reach the user. With Menlo Agent Runtime Security (MARS), that protection now extends to the AI agents working alongside every employee. Menlo Security is trusted by major global businesses, including Fortune 500 companies and government agencies, to protect their most valuable asset, their data, and is backed by top-tier investors.

About the Role

Summary

Menlo Security is building MARS for Agents (Menlo Agent Runtime Security), our product line for securing autonomous and hybrid AI agents. This is a category still being defined — standards, architecture patterns, and competitive positioning are all forming in real time, with competitors ranging from established network security vendors to a wave of new agent-security startups.

 

We are hiring an experienced Product Manager / Product Owner to take end-to-end ownership of a significant, technically complex area within MARS for Agents. The specific scope will be defined in partnership with the hiring manager based on team needs and the background of the person in this role, and will span identity and security concepts, relevant technical protocols, and platform integration and partnership work. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy day to day, working from strategic direction set by the Head of Product, in an environment that runs agile development at high velocity while actively building the process and rigor needed to scale a growing product line.

 

This is also a team that works the way it builds: AI assistants and LLM-based tools are part of the daily toolkit here — used to synthesize customer and competitive signal, pressure-test requirements, and prototype against MCP clients and agent runtimes before a single line of production code is written. The person in this role will be defining security for a category they are already a fluent, curious user of.

Outcomes & KPIs

Key Outcome(s) Owned:

  • End-to-end ownership of an assigned surface area of MARS for Agents — across capabilities such as the agent registry, Claude integration, Microsoft Copilot integration, MCP Server, MCP Proxy, and LLM proxy — from researched opportunity, to written requirement, to shipped and supported capability.

  • A current, honest, decision-changing competitive point of view for the agent-security category that the wider go-to-market organization can rely on.

Success Metrics / KPIs

  • Roadmap delivery: committed roadmap items for the owned surfaces shipped within the target release window.

  • Requirements quality: Reduction in mid-sprint requirement clarifications and rework attributable to ambiguous PRDs or acceptance criteria, measured via engineering feedback each quarter.

  • Enablement coverage: 100% of shipped capabilities in the owned area have current capability documentation and a delivered briefing to support and solutions engineering at or before release.

  • Adoption of shipped capability: Customer adoption or usage of newly released capabilities against a target set at launch, tracked for 90 days post-release.

  • Competitive influence: At least one documented roadmap or positioning decision per quarter, traceable to a published competitive finding.

What You'll Do

  • Own inbound product direction for your area. Research emerging agentic AI capabilities, attacker techniques, and adjacent standards (MCP, A2A, OWASP agentic-security guidance, agent identity frameworks) to determine what MARS for Agents should build next across the agent registry, Claude integration, Microsoft Copilot integration, MCP Server, MCP Proxy, and LLM proxy.

  • Turn signal into engineering-ready requirements. Translate market, customer, and competitive input into clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria — using LLM-based tools to synthesize call notes, support tickets, standards documents, and usage data into prioritization insight, while retaining full accountability for the judgment calls and the accuracy of what you write.

  • Own and groom the backlog. Make day-to-day prioritization calls across your surfaces within the strategic guardrails set by the Head of Product, and partner directly with engineering through the full build cycle: refinement, in-sprint questions, review, and release.

  • Validate before you specify. Use AI coding assistants, MCP clients, and agent runtimes hands-on to prototype and stress-test proposed behavior — so requirements are grounded in how agents actually behave, not just how they are documented to behave. Define success metrics for what you ship and track them post-release.

  • Enable the field. Brief technical support and solutions engineering on new and existing capabilities, and maintain current capability documentation for your area that clearly separates documented and shipping facts from planned work and open questions, so the field never over-promises. Be the trusted authority on what your part of MARS does today, what is coming, and what it deliberately does not do yet.

  • Engage customers, sales, and marketing. Join customer and prospect conversations periodically to gather requirements, pressure-test positioning, and support technical evaluations; support the sales team with technical Q&A, competitive objection-handling, and input on proposals and decks; and work with product marketing on messaging, positioning, and launch content.

  • Run competitive analysis that changes decisions. Continuously track competitors relevant to MARS for Agents — network/SSE-SASE incumbents (Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Cloudflare, Netskope), agent-identity and IAM players (Okta, CyberArk), MCP gateway vendors, and emerging agent-security pure-plays — and maintain a clear point of view on where MARS leads, where it currently trails, and what capabilities are commoditizing. Feed those findings directly into requirements, positioning, and roadmap prioritization.

Functional Competencies

Required:

  • 6–10+ years of product management or product owner experience, ideally in B2B SaaS, enterprise infrastructure, or security software, including a track record of owning a complex, technical product area end to end.

  • Demonstrated ability to write clear, engineering-ready requirements (PRDs, user stories, acceptance criteria) and to own a backlog end to end for a technically complex product surface.

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy. This role receives strategic direction rather than daily instruction, and the person in it should be able to take a goal and drive it through research, requirements, engineering partnership, and launch across multiple related surfaces at once — with the support of a collaborative product and engineering team.

  • Comfort operating at high velocity. Our engineering organization runs agile at a fast cadence, and this role also helps bring the process and rigor needed to make the product scalable, so both muscles matter.

  • Solid working knowledge of AI agent technology: how LLMs and AI agents operate, the difference between autonomous and human-in-the-loop (hybrid) agents, tool and function calling, and — specifically — the MCP (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem (servers, clients, tool calls) at a depth sufficient to write requirements for an MCP Server and an MCP Proxy, not just discuss them conceptually.

  • Real cybersecurity background, with working familiarity in areas such as identity and access management, proxy and gateway architectures (forward proxy, reverse proxy, secure web gateway / SSE / SASE), and content or traffic inspection. Deep specialization in every area is not required, but enough fluency to engage credibly with engineering and with technical customers is.

  • Hands-on, regular personal use of AI tools — for example Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code / Cowork, GitHub Copilot, or similar — including some exposure to how they use MCP or other tool-calling integrations.

  • Strong written communication, since the role produces a steady stream of specs, FAQs, and internal enablement material.

Preferred / Nice to Have:

  • Working knowledge of the Microsoft 365 Copilot ecosystem: M365 Copilot, Copilot Studio agents, and Microsoft's Entra/Azure agent identity plane — enough to scope and write requirements for a two-way integration in which MARS augments Microsoft's own agent governance rather than competing with it.

  • Prior product ownership of an identity or registry system, a proxy or gateway product, or an API/integration platform.

  • Direct experience with MCP, LLM/agent tool-calling architectures, or building integrations with Claude or other frontier model providers.

  • Familiarity with OWASP frameworks, including emerging OWASP guidance for agentic AI security.

  • Experience directly supporting a technical sales motion — SE enablement, competitive battlecards, customer discovery calls.

  • Experience at a company scaling a new product line or product category from early traction.

  • Experience using AI-assisted research or analysis tooling as part of a regular product workflow — for example synthesizing customer feedback at volume, or building lightweight prototypes to validate requirements.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Menlo Mindsets

The Menlo Mindsets serve as our strategic operating system, directly linking our daily behaviors to the business results we need to achieve by defining exactly "how" we do our work. By establishing this clear, shared standard, they empower our most successful employees to consistently drive the innovation and accountability required for our long-term success.

  • United Impact — I break down barriers to champion cross-functional collaboration, uniting diverse strengths with clear ownership to drive exceptional, aligned outcomes.

  • Customer-Compelled — Customer focus is my mission. I own their experience, prevent their challenges, and act with urgency to deliver value.

Menlo Security's mission: Enabling humans and agents to connect, communicate, and collaborate securely without compromise. title: Electrical Engineer II (Integrations)
description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

  • Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

The Launcher team is seeking a dedicated hardware engineer to own electronics design end-to-end and accelerate the path to production milestones.

Ideal candidate

A senior hardware engineer who has designed and shipped complex PCBs, ideally mixing digital and significant power (hundreds of watts), into production. They are rigorous on schematics, layout, and bring-up, and have a strong instinct for cost and manufacturability. They design with real-world operating conditions in mind - temperature, moisture, surges - and an interest in battery thermal management; direct experience of outdoor-deployed equipment is a plus rather than a prerequisite. They are comfortable working autonomously in a small team and can bridge hardware and firmware.

Skills required

  • PCB schematic and layout design (Altium Designer preferred)

  • Power electronics design: ~300 W DC/DC conversion, protection, derating, efficiency and thermal budgets

  • Thermal regulation: temperature sensing and control loops, battery storage temperature management, heatsinking

  • Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt): combined power and data delivery, isolation, cable budgets

  • Mixed-signal design: power management, MCU interfaces, communication buses (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, CAN, Ethernet)

  • Hardware bring-up and debug: bench equipment proficiency

  • DFM/DFA for PCB manufacturing and assembly

  • Component selection and BOM management

  • Experience in lightning and surge protection is a plus

Responsibilities:

  • Schematic Design - Design complete schematics for mixed-signal and power boards, from power stages to digital and communication sections.

  • PCB Layout & Routing - Perform or lead board placement and routing with attention to signal integrity, EMC, and power-path constraints.

  • Power & Thermal Architecture - Define and validate the power architecture of the product and the thermal strategy, including battery temperature management.

  • Environmental Robustness - Ensure the electronics withstand outdoor deployment conditions and define the associated qualification plan.

  • Component Selection & BOM Optimization - Select components with cost, availability, and reliability in mind; drive BOM cost reduction for mass production volumes.

  • Hardware Bring-up & Debug - Lead board bring-up, debug issues with oscilloscopes, power bench equipment, and other bench equipment; write bring-up scripts when needed.

  • EMC & Safety Compliance - Address EMC challenges; ensure signal integrity across the board and electrical safety of the power and battery sections.

  • Collaboration with Embedded SW - Work closely with the embedded software engineer to define hardware/software interfaces; support firmware bring-up.

  • Collaboration with Mechanical - Ensure seamless PCB integration into mechanical enclosures (connectors, mounting, thermal, sealing, shielding).

title: Strategic Account Executive - Paris
Senior Data Collection Operator (FR)
description:
About Genesis

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

The role

General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too.

You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area.

You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently.

What you will do

  • Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively.

  • Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering.

  • Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models.

  • Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data.

  • Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators.

  • Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy.

  • Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements.

  • Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar.

  • Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team.

  • Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues.

  • Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar.

What we are looking for

  • You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment.

  • Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach.

  • You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure.

  • You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering.

  • You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why.

  • You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team.

  • You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback.

  • You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off.

  • You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting.

  • You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works.

  • You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus.

  • Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing.

Working conditions and role constraints

  • Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories.

  • Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods.

  • Handling and lifting of loads, including props, fixtures, robot equipment, and station equipment, up to 23 kg for station setup and reconfiguration.

Why this role

  • Real ownership. You will have meaningful ownership over how the Paris data collection floor operates and help set the standard the team grows toward.

  • Hands-on leadership. You will remain close to the work while helping guide other operators, improve execution, and raise the quality bar.

  • Build, not just execute. You will take ambiguous collection needs and turn them into reliable, repeatable tasks that can scale across the team.

  • A clear growth path. As the operation scales, this role can grow toward leading or supervising teams of operators or toward broader project and program management responsibilities.

  • The front line of the mission. The data you create, review, and improve is what teaches our robots to work.

L'entreprise compte parmi les leaders mondiaux de son secteur et dessert des fabricants de parfums, de cosmétiques, de produits alimentaires et de boissons, ainsi que l'industrie pharmaceutique et les producteurs de compléments nutritionnels et d'aliments pour animaux.

Vos missions

Rattaché(e) au Secrétaire Général, avec un rattachement fonctionnel au Regional Head of Safety EAME, vous définissez, pilotez et faites évoluer la stratégie EHS du site de Clichy.

Véritable partenaire de la Direction du site et des responsables opérationnels, vous veillez à intégrer pleinement les enjeux EHS aussi bien dans les activités quotidiennes que dans les projets de transformation, de développement et d'investissement du site.

Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes :

  • Définir et déployer la stratégie EHS du site de Clichy, en cohérence avec les objectifs EHS globaux de Symrise et les priorités du business.

  • Manager et développer l'équipe EHS, en définissant les priorités et en veillant à disposer des compétences et ressources nécessaires.

  • Identifier, évaluer et prioriser les principaux risques environnementaux, santé et sécurité, et assurer la mise en œuvre de plans de prévention adaptés.

  • Intégrer les exigences EHS dès les premières étapes des projets de transformation, immobiliers, laboratoires et de développement du site.

  • Piloter la conformité réglementaire et anticiper les évolutions de la réglementation française et européenne en matière d'EHS susceptibles d'impacter les activités du site.

Vous êtes diplômé(e) d'une formation supérieure en Hygiène, Sécurité et Environnement (HSE/EHS), sciences environnementales, ingénierie ou dans un domaine connexe.

Vous justifiez d'au moins 10 ans d'expérience progressive dans une fonction EHS, idéalement acquise au sein d'une organisation internationale et dans des environnements complexes combinant activités industrielles, laboratoires ou opérations.

Au-delà de votre expertise technique, nous recherchons un profil capable d'allier vision stratégique et pragmatisme opérationnel.

  • Une solide expertise en management EHS, évaluation des risques et conformité réglementaire.

Ce poste vous offre l'opportunité de prendre la responsabilité des enjeux EHS au sein d'un site stratégique de Symrise, en collaboration étroite avec la Direction locale ainsi qu'avec les équipes régionales et globales du Groupe.

Troostwijk & the TBAuctions group are part of one of Europe’s leading networks for digital B2B auctions. We market machines, vehicles, equipment and other commercial assets, bringing sellers and buyers together through digital processes and personal support.

As an Account Manager, you will develop the French seller market and act as the main point of contact for new and existing sellers.   • Represent our company image and values in the market and coordinate closely with internal teams.
What matters in this role

  • Willingness to travel regularly and a valid Category B driving licence.

A perfect CV is less important than your ability to create relationships, develop a territory and turn commercial opportunities into long-term seller business.

Autonomy with professional support

You will own your territory and your seller relationships while working closely with internal teams that support you with expertise, coordination and operational follow-through. You will not be left alone with complex opportunities or process questions.

Build something with visible impact

The role gives you the opportunity to help establish the French market, shape long-term seller relationships and contribute directly to recurring auction activity. Your work combines commercial ownership with professional development.

Performance that pays off

You can expect an attractive compensation package with a competitive fixed salary and a bonus model that recognises your individual performance.

Your benefits

Company car, computer, phone and meal tickets support you in your day-to-day work.

title: Location Data engineer
description:
We are seeking a highly skilled Location Data Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will work with large-scale datasets generated by our products and turn raw data into meaningful signals, insights, and features.

You will work across the entire data lifecycle: building reliable pipelines, exploring and understanding complex datasets, developing features from them, and creating the tools and visualizations needed to understand their quality and impact.

This is a technical and product-oriented data role. You'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, and data teams to find what we can learn from our data and turn those learnings into production systems.

As a Data Engineer, your day-to-day will include:

  • Making Sense of Data

    • Explore large and complex datasets to understand user behavior and identify useful patterns and signals.

    • Transform raw data into reliable, well-defined features that can be used by our products and engineering teams.

    • Develop a deep understanding of our data: where it comes from, what it represents, its limitations, and how it can be combined to answer new questions.

  • Building Data Products

    • Design, build, and maintain pipelines that process large volumes of data efficiently and reliably.

    • Take ideas from exploration to production: prototype them on historical data, evaluate their quality, and build the pipelines needed to run them at scale.

    • Build datasets and features that can power product experiences, internal systems, analytics, and machine learning models.

    • Work with technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or similar tools depending on the problem at hand.

  • Exploring & Analyzing

    • Use data to investigate hypotheses, understand behaviors, and answer ambiguous questions.

    • Develop metrics and evaluation frameworks to understand whether the signals and features we build actually work.

    • Create analyses, dashboards, and visualizations that make complex datasets understandable and help the team make better decisions.

    • Build tooling that makes it easier to inspect individual examples, debug data pipelines, and understand why a system produces a particular result.

  • From Data to Intelligence

    • Work closely with engineers and product teams to identify opportunities where data can make our products smarter.

    • Use statistical methods, heuristics, experimentation, or machine learning depending on what is most appropriate for the problem.

    • Iterate on features and models based on real-world data and continuously improve their accuracy and reliability.

    • Help bridge the gap between exploratory data work and robust systems running in production.

  • Continuous Improvement

    • Improve the performance, reliability, and maintainability of our data infrastructure.

    • Monitor data quality and proactively investigate unexpected changes or anomalies.

    • Stay up to date with developments in data engineering, analytics, and machine learning, and bring relevant ideas and technologies into our stack.

    • Contribute to a culture of curiosity, craftsmanship, and learning.

Your Skills & Experience

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience working with data-intensive systems.

  • Very comfortable with SQL and manipulating large datasets.

  • Experience with one or more modern data technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or equivalent tools.

  • Strong analytical skills: you enjoy digging into data, testing hypotheses, and understanding why something behaves the way it does.

  • Ability to turn exploratory analysis into reliable, production-ready data pipelines and features.

  • Familiarity with data modeling, pipeline orchestration, and large-scale data processing.

  • Ability to communicate findings clearly through metrics, visualizations, dashboards, or other tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building data products or features directly used by consumer-facing products.

  • Experience working with high-volume event, behavioral, sensor, geospatial, or time-series data.

  • Familiarity with statistics, machine learning, or feature engineering.

  • Experience taking a data problem from an ambiguous question through exploration, prototyping, evaluation, and production.

  • Experience building internal tools or visualizations for exploring and debugging complex datasets.

Life at amo

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

We chose a location in central Paris, near Opéra (Metro lines 3, 8, 9 and RER A).

We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

  • Health care (100% coverage).

  • Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

  • Vacation days: 8–9 weeks (total) per year:

  • 5 weeks of paid time off;

  • 1–2 additional weeks (RTT, based on our company contract);

  • ~11 bank holidays.

We shut down entirely twice a year, two weeks in summer and one week in winter, to allow everyone to truly recharge and avoid prolonged slowdowns. These pauses are part of your total vacation time, giving everyone a real chance to unplug and recharge. No Slack, no email, no FOMO.

We love the diverse perspectives we get from having people from all over the world join us (68% of our team is international), and so we of course support relocation to Paris with:

  • Help and sponsored visa process.

  • 1 month of Airbnb 100% covered by amo upon arrival.

  • Assistance from a trusted relocation agency to find your permanent home.

  • Help with French paperwork like opening a French social security account, tax forms, getting your carte vitale (free healthcare), and more.

  • French lessons to be fully set with your new Parisian life.

😕 Probably not a fit

About The Opportunity

We are building a rigorous, verifiable evaluation suite of Terminal-Bench tasks designed to test the limits of large language models on multilingual software challenges. Our goal is to measure multilingual robustness across prompt language effects, non-English data processing, and complex locale/encoding edge cases in terminal workflows.

We are seeking experienced native-speaking software engineers to design, build, and validate these benchmarks. You will create high-signal, high-quality tasks that genuinely test a model's ability to handle multilingual environments without relying on English translation crutches.

  • Prompting & Translation: finding failure points where AI does not work, in your native language

  • Implementation & Verification: Support the development of robust solutions (reference implementations) and write highly reliable, deterministic verifier scripts (using rubric-based judging only when strictly necessary).

  • Calibration & Execution: Analyze execution logs and calibrate task difficulty (Easy to Very Hard) using standard Terminal-Bench run configurations against various model tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus).

  • Quality Assurance: Participate in a rigorous, 4-layer human quality control process (creation, human review, calibration review, and audit) alongside automated LLM-based checks to ensure fairness, grammatical accuracy, and benchmark integrity.

title: Platform Deployment Engineer (Europe)
description:
Neural Concept embeds AI into design and simulation workflows so engineering teams make continuous, data-driven decisions instead of waiting on sequential design–simulation–validation cycles. None of that matters until the platform is running inside the customer's environment, on their infrastructure, under their rules.


That is this role. You take an enterprise customer and make the platform real for them: architected, deployed, integrated, cleared by their security organisation, and stable enough that their engineers stop thinking about it. You own that outcome end to end for named accounts, as their primary technical counterpart.

 

What you will do

  • The deployment, from the first architecture conversation through go-live and into steady-state operation.

  • Its integration with the customer's identity, data and engineering systems, and the infrastructure and model serving layer beneath it.

  • The relationship with their IT, security and platform teams: assessments, architecture reviews, and the call when something breaks.

  • The diagnosis when it does break, including when the cause sits outside our own software.

  • The runbooks, post-mortems and playbooks that make the next deployment easier, and the feedback loop into Product.

 

Where you will do it
Managed Kubernetes across the major clouds. On-premises and fully air-gapped clusters with no route to the internet, GPU infrastructure, self-hosted model serving. Customer HPC environments, schedulers, and shared storage under real load.

 

If installing software with no internet access, on hardware you do not control, reads as the interesting part of the job rather than the obstacle, this will suit you.

 

Who you are

You will often be the only Neural Concept engineer in the room. We are looking for someone with:

  • 6+ years deploying and operating enterprise software in production, two of them in environments you did not control.

  • Kubernetes at configuration depth: how chart values become rendered manifests, and why a workload will not start.

  • Identity and SSO fundamentals: OIDC and SAML, clients and credential rotation, redirect URIs, group-to-role mapping.

  • Linux, networking and TLS: DNS, routing, ingress and egress, certificate chains and interception proxies.

  • Kubernetes storage: persistent volumes and CSI, access modes, diagnosing shared storage that degrades under load.

  • Professional customer-facing English, and willingness to travel and work your customers' hours.

Also valuable: regulated or air-gapped deployments · private registries and image mirroring · GPU scheduling and LLM serving · enterprise IdP administration · Terraform and GitOps · Prometheus and Grafana · HPC schedulers · ISO 27001 evidence · Python · PLM, CAD or CAE exposure.

 

You Get

Where You Will Be

title: Software Test Engineer 80–100%
description:
About machineMD

At machineMD in Bern we’re on a mission to radically improve the measurement of brain function through standardized, automated, quantitative exams. Our signature product, neos™, is the world’s first non-invasive neuro-ophthalmoscope for fast, automated assessment of eye movements and pupils. Founded at the University Hospital of Bern, Switzerland, we’ve grown into a startup of 25 engineers, clinicians, scientists, and specialists working side by side. We aim to bring the diagnostic quality of highly trained specialists into secondary and primary care settings everywhere.

We’re building neurodiagnostics for the next generation with our neos™ device and oculometrics software. As our Software Test Engineer, you’ll have room to make a visible difference in how we test. Find a gap, develop an approach, and put it to work, whether that means automating a manual check, building better test data, or connecting tests across the system. You’ll develop our test automation with support from developers, requirements engineers, and testers. Our existing test infrastructure gives you a starting point, with room to introduce your own ideas and additional tools as you connect and improve how we test.

The Role

You’ll help us understand how neos™ behaves when its components work together—and where they fail. Your main contribution will be developing automated tests, test data, and scripts that make complex scenarios repeatable and problems easier to diagnose. You’ll work alongside developers and use the domain expertise and manual testing provided by requirements engineers and testers.

  • Pragmatic Improvements – assess our current testing setup with the team, identify the biggest weaknesses, and tackle them step by step. Build on what works, try useful approaches, and let a broader test concept grow from the improvements you put into practice.

  • Automation Across the System – develop automated tests for complex, distributed systems across different frameworks and technologies, covering multiple components, interfaces, and end-to-end scenarios beyond UI testing.

  • Test Infrastructure – build on and improve our physical and software-based test environments. Introduce tools and setups where they make testing more effective, and keep them documented so tests remain repeatable and usable by others.

  • Coordination & Code Quality – work hands-on with developers to implement automation, coordinate contributions, and review the quality of test code. Connect individual improvements so our testing becomes more consistent and easier to extend over time.

  • Verification & Validation – contribute to V&V plans, protocols, reports, and evidence, and coordinate activities with the relevant specialists. Help keep testing, requirements, and documentation aligned in a medical device environment.

What We Look For

Experience

  • Solid practical experience in software engineering, including designing, implementing, debugging, and maintaining software. You can understand existing codebases and develop clear, well-structured solutions that others can maintain and extend.

  • Experience with some of our core technologies (Python, C#/.NET, C++ and Flutter/Dart) is a plus. Python and pytest are particularly useful for test automation, and you’re willing to learn the technologies needed for the task.

  • Practical experience developing automated tests across different system levels, with the programming skills to implement, understand, and review test code.

  • Experience with verification and validation of medical devices or familiarity with ISO 13485 is a plus.

Qualifications

  • Solid software testing fundamentals at ISTQB Foundation Level or equivalent knowledge, including test planning, test design, and requirements coverage.

  • Vocational training or a higher degree in computer science, software engineering, medical informatics, or a related technical field.

  • Fluent English (minimum strong B2, ideally C1); German or French language skills are a plus for on-site collaboration.

How You Work

  • Systems Thinker – you want to understand how neos™ works as a whole, from its software and hardware to the tests and data behind it. you choose practical improvements as our product and testing continue to develop.

  • Curiosity & a Detective’s Instinct – you notice when something doesn’t quite add up and enjoy following the clues. You question assumptions, explore unusual scenarios, and keep digging until you can explain and reproduce what you’ve found.

  • Close the Gaps – you enjoy getting your hands dirty and following a problem across disciplines. When progress depends on something outside your usual remit, you’re willing to learn, lend a hand.

  • Collaborative Spirit – you work closely with colleagues, share what you know and what you’re unsure about, and address difficult topics openly. You listen with curiosity, give and receive candid feedback, and make room for different perspectives.

  • Shaper Mentality & Growth Mindset – you want to shape how testing works, take responsibility, and build missing skills quickly. You’re curious about neurodiagnostics and ready to learn from experts and real-world use cases.

Working at machineMD

  • Based in Bern, Switzerland, with roughly 80% of your working time on-site (approximately four days a week at full-time employment) and Monday as our shared anchor day.

  • Collaborative, in-person working, with flexibility to do your best work.

Our Four Pillars of Integrity guide how we work together:

  • Radical Responsibility: Own our choices.

  • Feeling Our Feelings: Name and honour our emotions.

  • Candor: Speak and listen with honesty.

  • Clear Agreements: Make and keep clear commitments.

Life’s too short to work on boring stuff. If you want to connect ideas, people, and technology to advance brain diagnostics in a dynamic startup, let’s talk!

How to Apply

Send your CV and a short note about a project or task from your career that you enjoyed a lot, and explain why.

We welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of gender, age, background, or orientation. Direct applications only, no recruiters please.

We’re excited to meet you!
